source.method: chapter titles from each book's Contents page, books in the order History, Geography, Political Science, Economics; topics from each chapter PDF's section headings (numbered in History; unnumbered, sometimes run-in, in the other three books; a short lead-in heading is folded into the next topic; exercises are not topics; some topics come from titled boxes, for example Project Tiger, Bamboo Drip Irrigation System, Bhoodan - Gramdan and Popular participation in political parties)

chapters.title: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
chapters.book: India and the Contemporary World - II

topics.title: The French Revolution and the Idea of the Nation
objectives: Student can describe Sorrieu's vision of a world of democratic and social republics
Student can list the measures French revolutionaries took to create a sense of collective identity, such as la patrie, le citoyen and the tricolour
Student can explain the main changes of the Napoleonic Code of 1804 and the mixed reactions to French rule in conquered areas
visualIdeas: Sorrieu's print of peoples marching towards the Statue of Liberty
a list of revolutionary measures: flag, anthem, uniform laws, weights and measures

topics.title: The Making of Nationalism in Europe
objectives: Student can explain why there were no nation-states in Germany, Italy and Switzerland in the mid-eighteenth century
Student can describe the diversity of peoples and languages within the Habsburg Empire
visualIdeas: a map of Europe in 1797 with many small states

topics.title: The Aristocracy and the New Middle Class
objectives: Student can describe the aristocracy as the dominant class, united by a common way of life
Student can explain how industrialisation created a working class and a middle class that supported national unity
visualIdeas: a social pyramid of aristocracy, middle class and peasants

topics.title: What did Liberal Nationalism Stand for?
objectives: Student can explain what liberalism meant for the middle classes: individual freedom, equality before law and government by consent
Student can explain why voting rights were limited to property-owning men
Student can explain how the Zollverein of 1834 promoted economic unity in the German states
visualIdeas: a customs barrier being lifted between German states

topics.title: A New Conservatism after 1815
objectives: Student can describe the aims of the Treaty of Vienna (1815) hosted by Duke Metternich
Student can explain how conservative regimes curbed liberty through censorship
visualIdeas: a map of Europe after the Congress of Vienna

topics.title: The Revolutionaries
objectives: Student can describe secret societies formed by liberal-nationalists after 1815
Student can explain Giuseppe Mazzini's ideas and why Metternich called him the most dangerous enemy of the social order
visualIdeas: portrait of Mazzini with Young Italy and Young Europe labels

topics.title: The Age of Revolutions: 1830-1848
objectives: Student can describe the July Revolution of 1830 in France and Belgium's break from the Netherlands
Student can explain how the Greek war of independence mobilised nationalist feelings across Europe
visualIdeas: a timeline of revolts from 1821 to 1848

topics.title: The Romantic Imagination and National Feeling
objectives: Student can explain how Romanticism used folk culture, music and language to create national feeling
Student can explain Herder's idea of the spirit of the nation (volksgeist) and the importance of language, using Poland as an example
visualIdeas: Grimm's fairy tale book next to a folk musician

topics.title: Hunger, Hardship and Popular Revolt
objectives: Student can explain the economic hardship in Europe in the 1830s and the revolt of the Silesian weavers
Student can describe the 1848 revolution of the liberals and the Frankfurt Parliament
Student can explain why the Frankfurt Parliament failed and the reforms monarchs introduced after 1848
visualIdeas: the Frankfurt parliament in the Church of St Paul

topics.title: Germany - Can the Army be the Architect of a Nation?
objectives: Student can explain how Prussia under Otto von Bismarck unified Germany through three wars
Student can describe the proclamation of Kaiser William I at Versailles in January 1871
visualIdeas: the Hall of Mirrors ceremony
a map of German unification

topics.title: Italy Unified
objectives: Student can explain how Italians were scattered over several dynastic states and the Habsburg Empire
Student can explain the roles of Mazzini, Cavour and Garibaldi in unifying Italy and how Victor Emmanuel II was proclaimed king in 1861
Student can explain why much of the Italian population, with high illiteracy, remained unaware of liberal-nationalist ideology
visualIdeas: a map of Italian states before unification

topics.title: The Strange Case of Britain
objectives: Student can explain how the British nation was formed through a long process rather than a sudden revolution
Student can describe the Act of Union 1707 and the incorporation of Ireland in 1801
Student can name symbols of the new Britain such as the Union Jack and the English language
visualIdeas: the Union Jack made from three crosses

topics.title: Visualising the Nation
objectives: Student can explain how artists personified nations as female figures
Student can describe Marianne and Germania and the meaning of their symbols
visualIdeas: Marianne and Germania side by side
a table of symbols and their meanings

topics.title: Nationalism and Imperialism
objectives: Student can explain how nationalism became narrow and aggressive after 1871
Student can explain why the Balkans became the source of tension leading to the First World War
Student can explain how nationalism joined with imperialism and later inspired anti-imperial movements
visualIdeas: a map of the Balkans with rival powers

chapters.title: Nationalism in India
chapters.book: India and the Contemporary World - II

visualIdeas: a walled garden with a narrow exit

topics.title: Why Non-cooperation?

visualIdeas: a staircase of non-cooperation stages

visualIdeas: Ambedkar and Gandhi with the Poona Pact

topics.title: The Sense of Collective Belonging
objectives: Student can explain how the image of Bharat Mata, from Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's Vande Mataram to Abanindranath Tagore's painting, gave the nation an identity

visualIdeas: Abanindranath Tagore's Bharat Mata
a flag with a spinning wheel

chapters.title: The Making of a Global World
chapters.book: India and the Contemporary World - II

topics.title: The Pre-modern World
objectives: Student can explain that the making of the global world has a long history of trade, migration, movement of people and exchange of ideas
Student can give early examples of links between distant regions, such as Indus valley trade with West Asia and cowries from the Maldives
visualIdeas: cowrie shells travelling from the Maldives to distant markets

topics.title: Silk Routes Link the World
objectives: Student can describe the silk routes linking Asia with Europe and northern Africa and the goods carried along them
Student can explain how missionaries and preachers also travelled these routes, so trade and cultural exchange went together
visualIdeas: a map of land and sea silk routes across Asia, Europe and Africa

topics.title: Food Travels: Spaghetti and Potato
objectives: Student can explain how foods such as noodles travelled and how crops like potatoes, maize, tomatoes and chillies reached the rest of the world from America
Student can explain how the potato improved the diet of Europe's poor and why Ireland suffered a famine when the potato crop failed in the mid-1840s
visualIdeas: a plate of spaghetti and a potato with arrows showing their journeys

topics.title: Conquest, Disease and Trade
objectives: Student can explain how the world shrank after European sailors found a sea route to Asia and crossed the ocean to America in the sixteenth century
Student can explain how American silver enriched Europe and how germs such as smallpox helped the Spanish conquest
Student can explain why, until the eighteenth century, China and India were among the world's richest countries and how the centre of world trade shifted west
visualIdeas: a European ship crossing the Atlantic towards America

topics.title: The Nineteenth Century (1815-1914)
objectives: Student can name the three flows of international economic exchange: trade, labour and capital
Student can explain how these flows were interwoven in the nineteenth century
visualIdeas: three arrows labelled goods, people and money circling the globe

topics.title: A World Economy Takes Shape
objectives: Student can explain why the abolition of the Corn Laws made Britain import food and how British agriculture was affected
Student can explain how lands in America and Australia were cleared, railways and ports built, and people migrated to meet the demand for food
Student can describe the canal colonies of west Punjab as an example of this change in India
visualIdeas: a flow chart from the Corn Laws ending to migration across the Atlantic

topics.title: Role of Technology
objectives: Student can explain the role of railways, steamships and the telegraph in transforming the nineteenth-century world

visualIdeas: a refrigerated ship carrying frozen meat from Australia to Europe

topics.title: Late nineteenth-century Colonialism

visualIdeas: a map of Africa with straight colonial borders

visualIdeas: a map of rinderpest moving across Africa like forest fire
